original_description: Set up a fresh practice copy of the claim tagger's editor feedback loop in Notion and guide an editor through it: one command creates a new page under a page the editor picks, with its own one-tag rulebook (Context-dependent), seven real claims, a small decision queue, a rule-changes table and seven numbered steps, then says where the editor is and what to type next. Use this skill whenever someone wants to try, learn, practise, demo or teach the claim tagger or the editorial feedback loop, onboard a new editor, make a training or practice page, or asks "where am I in the walkthrough/demo", even if they never say "walkthrough". It never touches real claims or the real rulebook; for real tagging, distilling or promoting use /claim-tagger.

final_description: Use this skill for anything about a practice, training or demo copy of the claim tagger in Notion: creating one (a fresh walkthrough page under a Notion page or link the user gives, a sandbox to show the team how tagging, editor decisions and rule-change approval work, a page to onboard or train a new editor), starting another once the last one is finished, and asking where they are or what the next step is in a practice run, walkthrough or demo. Each practice page is a self-contained sandbox with its own one-tag rulebook, seven claims, a decision queue and seven numbered steps, so learners never touch real data. Prefer this over /claim-tagger whenever the request is about practising, training, demoing, onboarding, a walkthrough, or showing someone how the loop works. Not for real work: tagging this week's claims, the agent's status, distilling, promoting or rolling back real rule changes, editing the taxonomy, or archiving pages.
